items.title: Augmented ABC tolerance target
items.statement: For a prior and simulator on standard Borel spaces, define the joint prior-simulator measure restricted to the summary-tolerance event and normalize it only when the event has positive probability.

items.title: The augmented ABC target has the tolerance posterior as its parameter marginal
items.statement: When the tolerance-event probability is positive, the parameter marginal of the augmented ABC target equals the tolerance-conditioned parameter law defined by the simulator-based ABC interface.

items.title: ABC Metropolis–Hastings on simulator-augmented states
items.statement: At a fixed tolerance with positive prior-predictive acceptance probability, run the general Metropolis–Hastings procedure on the augmented parameter-simulator state using a proposal that perturbs the parameter and simulates new data.

items.title: Sequential ABC importance-resampling with tolerance populations
items.statement: For a decreasing finite sequence of positive tolerances, resample ancestors from the current weighted population, perturb and simulate once per child, then weight tolerance matches by a finite nonnegative version of the prior-to-proposal-mixture Radon–Nikodym derivative when the mixture dominates the prior; nonmatches receive zero weight.

items.title: ABC Metropolis–Hastings preserves its augmented tolerance target
items.statement: For a fixed positive tolerance, positive normalizer, standard Borel augmented state space, and probability proposal kernel, the ABC-MH kernel is reversible with respect to and leaves invariant the augmented ABC target.

items.title: Sequential ABC Radon–Nikodym weights target each tolerance law
items.statement: Conditionally on any previous weighted population whose proposal mixture dominates the prior, the accepted ABC proposal reweighted by the prior-to-mixture Radon–Nikodym derivative has the normalized tolerance target as its population-level weighted law; resampling preserves the weighted empirical mean conditionally.

title: ABC-MCMC and ABC-sequential Monte Carlo — Examples

items.title: ABC acceptance probability vanishes with the tolerance
items.statement: A continuous uniform simulator has positive ABC acceptance probability for every positive tolerance but acceptance probability tending to zero as the tolerance shrinks to zero, where the indicator target is undefined.

items.title: A positive-tolerance ABC-MH stationary law can differ from the exact-data posterior
items.statement: A finite simulator with a non-sufficient summary has an explicit positive-tolerance augmented ABC target and independence-proposal ABC-MH kernel that leaves it invariant, while its parameter marginal differs from the exact-data posterior.

items.title: A finite ABC-SMC tolerance schedule and its mixture weights
items.statement: For a two-parameter finite simulator, calculate two positive decreasing tolerance targets, the proposal-mixture acceptance probability, Radon–Nikodym weights, and the normalized target parameter marginal from the expected unnormalized weights, while distinguishing it from the realized finite-particle self-normalized estimate.

items.title: Finite ABC-SMC particles can miss target support despite a valid mixture weight
items.statement: Even when the ABC proposal mixture dominates the prior and all Radon–Nikodym weights are valid, a finite population can miss a positive-mass target component and collapse to an unrepresentative repeated particle.
